title: PRD Dependency Orchestra: Scheduled Review Waves & Ownership Matrix
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective: Create a timeboxed, repeatable PRD review choreography that aligns engineering, design, and legal reviewers into three 'review waves' with clear owners, artifacts required, and explicit acceptance criteria. This ticket establishes the schedule template, owner matrix, per-team checklist, and escalation path to be used for mid-sized product PRDs (scope: multi-route API changes, Console UX updates, telemetry schema changes).

Motivation: Past PRD reviews have inconsistent reviewer availability and ambiguous handoffs, causing late-stage scope slippage and rework. We need a prescriptive cadence that reduces back-and-forth and surfaces legal/infra/security blockers earlier in the cycle.

Scope:
- Define 3 review waves: Wave 0 (Discovery & Safety), Wave 1 (Design + API semantics), Wave 2 (Engineering implementation & rollout).
- For each wave, specify required artifacts, owners, review duration, deliverables, and acceptance criteria.
- Produce a lightweight sign-off template (one-page) for cross-team acceptance and a short runbook for handling conflicting feedback.
- Produce a shared calendar invite template and a checklist for PRD authors.
- Integrate sign-off gates into the PRD Confluence template and record GitHub PR links for implementation traceability.

Wave definitions and owners:
- Wave 0 (Discovery & Safety, 3 business days): owners: PM (Ava Martinez), Security Rep (Jordan Lee), Legal Reviewer (Maya Singh). Required artifacts: risk summary, dataflow sketch, compliance flags. Acceptance criteria: list of compliance questions answered; no open high-severity legal blockers.
- Wave 1 (Design + API semantics, 4 business days): owners: Design Lead (Olivia Chen), API Lead (Diego Ramos). Required artifacts: high-fidelity mocks, API surface doc, example structured outputs, sample prompts/eval plan. Acceptance criteria: design accessibility checklist met; API contract versioned; example responses validated against eval set.
- Wave 2 (Engineering implementation & rollout, 5 business days): owners: ENG Owner (Liam O'Connor), Infra Owner (Priya Desai). Required artifacts: implementation plan, rollout timeline, migration plan, telemetry + alert spec. Acceptance criteria: implementation risks cataloged; rollout runbook with rollback criteria; telemetry hooks defined and dashboards linked.

Acceptance criteria (cross-wave):
- All waves must have either explicit sign-off or documented mitigation for any open items.
- Legal must sign or provide a mitigations PRD for privacy/regulatory risks.
- Security must confirm risk severity <= medium or provide compensating controls.
- Engineering must provide a realistic timeline and identify any infra capacity needs.
- Design must provide final mocks and a dev handoff Figma link.

Deliverables:
- One-page sign-off artifact attached to PRD (Confluence).
- Calendarized review windows with owners invited.
- Template checklist added to PRD template.
- Small automation: PRD checklist toggles required reviewers based on selected labels (API change, telemetry, private-deployment).

Escalation & tie-breakers:
- If reviewers disagree on a blocking decision, the PM escalates to the Review Arbiter (Head of Product, settings: Aaron Novak) who issues a decision within 48 hours.
- If legal/security require >5 business days, PM must either reduce scope or move to an approval sprint with documented reasons.

Success metrics:
- Reduce average PRD review cycle time from baseline by 35% within two quarters.
- Reduce last-minute scope churn flagged during implementation by 50% within one quarter.
- Track sign-off compliance rate and display in the Console "PRD health" dashboard.

Notes/Constraints:
- This template applies only to PRDs that touch production inference runtime, customer-facing Console flows, or telemetry/personal data changes.
- For Private/on-prem features, add infra compliance reviewer in Wave 0.
